newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets third record in a row; second biggest weekly gain.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets third record in a row; second biggest weekly gain.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average snared its second biggest weekly point gain ever Friday, capping post-election fireworks with still more record highs.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 13.78 points to 6,219.82, its third record close in a row. Its weekly gain of 197.89 points was the second biggest since the 206.77-point surge in the week of Aug. 2 this year.

The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks also set a record, gaining 3.17 points to 730.82, its fourth straight closing high. The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.41 to 386.32, a new high.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,191 to 1,089 on active volume of 402 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market drifted lower through most of the day but rebounded nicely late in the session.

"The stock market was down most of the day and then flipped back in the afternoon. It was a consolidation day after a big week for stocks and bonds," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Investors were in a bullish mood this week, stoked by Tuesday's national elections that produced the status-quo in Washington -- President Clinton in the White House and the Republicans in control of Congress.
Wall Street has done well in the past two years, with the Republicans keeping Clinton's spending priorities in check.
More of the same is hoped for. In his first news conference since winning re-election, Clinton Friday said balancing the budget was his top second-term priority.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost 10/32 to 6.51 percent.
The Treasuries market will be closed Monday for Veteran's Day but stock exchanges will hold a regular trading session.

Bond losses steepened Friday after September wholesale inventories fell 1.3 percent, the biggest drop since the 1.6 percent fall in February 1982. The data suggested inventories are fairly lean and could lead to a production pickup in the fourth quarter.
Next week's string of economic reports include producer prices for October, which are due on Wednesday and both consumer prices and retail sales on Thursday.
Benign inflation readings are expected, with the focus on retail sales for a preview of what may lie ahead for the important Christmas shopping season.
"People are more optimistic about Christmas," said Peter Cardillo director of research at Westfalia Investments.
But otherwise, the stock market is "sorting things out and coming to a reflection period. It's looking at future earnings, and what the future might be on the economy and interest rates," he said.
Among special situations, America Online rose 1-1/4 to 26. The world's largest online service reported in-line first- quarter earnings and a sharp gain in revenues.
Kellogg lost one to 66-3/4 on concerns about the cereal giant's market share and competitive pressures after it held a meeting with Wall Street analysts.

Odwalla shed 2-11/16 to 10-3/8. A 15-month-old girl died in Denver after drinking tainted apple juice. It was not known if the juice was from Odwalla but the company was notified by health officials that the child had been associated with the recent E. coli cases linked to Odwalla apple juice.
Mossimo lost 5-3/4 to 16-1/8 on disappointing results.
Conrail rose 3-1/4 to 96-1/4 after receiving a sweetened hostile $110 a share takeover bid from Norfolk Southern, whose stock lost 3/8 to 86-5/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 3.37 points at 1,257.51. The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.14 to 580.39. The NYSE average share was up 15 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a record 7,069.887 up 24.063 or 0.34 percent.
